system.summary: Numbered nomenclator 1-700 of 1757 (ANOM COL C11E 10): syllables, words and names, letters with homophones.

prior_solution.where: contemporary abstracts only (NY Col. Docs X 974-975, for 10 and 16 Apr 1759); LAC transcripts C-2401 skip ff. 54-76

conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout chose the target from the catalogue and set the rules (frozen key before validation, held-out checks, prior-work search the day of publication); AI agents transcribed, solved, checked and wrote up. Doubtful signs were settled by targeted visual review where stated.
models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agents run by Brice Dudout

solution.what: Period table ANOM C11E 10 (NFA 15213) transcribed (deciphering 1-700, checked on the enciphering table) and frozen as v1.
One measurement on the held-out glossed copy of 8 May 1759 (LAC C-2401): 0.972 vs best of 200 permuted keys 0.185.
The four letters decoded and read as sentences; 20 key values corrected in context (v2); Daniel's rule met for each letter.

outcome.method: read after matching with key from external sources
outcome.method_basis: Contemporary nomenclator "Chiffre avec M. le Mis de Vaudreuil ... 1757" (ANOM COL C11E 10 ff. 285-290v), transcribed and validated on a held-out letter with a contemporary decipherment.
outcome.fraction_read_source: Daniel's rule (certain + probable; restored words are not counted as read), counted word by word on reading_<n>.md: 4,345 cipher words, 4,142 certain, 60 probable, 119 restored, 24 unresolved = 96.7% (99.4% with the restored words). 1388: 2,012 words, 99.6%; 1389: 692, 97.7%; 1390: 210, 99.5%; 1391: 1,431, 91.8% (98.6% with restorations), so 1391 is read in part and the group is read in part.

validation.notes: Contributor's pre-registered held-out test (not docs/_validate.py): key v1 frozen, one measurement on the LAC copy of the 8 May 1759 cipher letter with its contemporary interlinear decipherment (1,134 groups): character agreement 0.9723 vs best of 200 permuted keys 0.1850 (mean 0.0957). Criterion fixed in advance: >= 0.85 and >= best control + 0.30.

credits.note: the 1757 cipher table "Chiffre avec M. le Mis de Vaudreuil", ANOM COL C11E 10 ff. 285-290v; and the contemporary interlinear decipherment of 8 May 1759 (LAC transcript C-2401) used as the validation control
period key ANOM C11E 10 transcribed and validated on a held-out glossed letter (0.972 vs 0.185); the four letters 1388-1391 transcribed, decrypted, read and translated

texts.label: Vaudreuil to the minister, Montréal, 8 April 1759 (ANOM COL C11A 104, ff. 54-66)
texts.summary: Vaudreuil reports the famine (four ounces of bread a day, cattle and horses almost gone), the militia census (Quebec 6,356, Montréal 5,455, Trois-Rivières 1,313 men) and his plan for 1759: hold Carillon, the Ohio (Lignery at Fort Machault after Fort Duquesne was blown up), Niagara (Pouchot) and La Présentation, two new corvettes on Lake Ontario; he sees Cumberland's old plan revived by Amherst; Quebec will be defended after the battle at Carillon; he asks for battalions, munitions and above all food, having taken the mills' meal and the tithes.

reading_review.note: Read as sentences 2026-11-04 against translation_1388.md: coherent French throughout. Word count: 2,012 words, 1,965 certain, 38 probable, 6 restored, 3 unresolved = 99.6% read as sense.

texts.label: Vaudreuil to the minister, Montréal, 10 April 1759 (ANOM COL C11A 104, ff. 68-72)
texts.summary: "For yourself alone": Montcalm's view that the colony is lost has become public, officers of the land troops speak against Vaudreuil before the people; he threatens to send the ringleaders to France, but humours Montcalm to avoid an open break and gives him the command of the army of Carillon.

reading_review.note: Read as sentences 2026-11-04 against translation_1389.md: coherent French throughout. Word count: 692 words, 669 certain, 7 probable, 15 restored, 1 unresolved = 97.7% read as sense.

texts.label: Vaudreuil to the minister, Montréal, 16 April 1759 (ANOM COL C11A 104, ff. 75-76)
texts.summary: Provisions: the contractor (munitionnaire) has his correspondents in France replace any captured supply ship at once; the freight is to be paid to the King in Canada; Vaudreuil asks again for a supplement of food, without which the colony would fall of itself.

reading_review.note: Read as sentences 2026-11-04 against translation_1390.md: coherent French throughout. Word count: 210 words, 205 certain, 4 probable, 1 restored, 0 unresolved = 99.5% read as sense.

texts.label: Vaudreuil to the minister, Montréal, 13 August 1760 (ANOM COL C11A 105, ff. 147-152)
texts.summary: Three weeks before the capitulation of Montréal: the ships and stores at Restigouche (Danjac) are in danger; the Machault (Lagiraudays) and the schooner l'Extravagante carry the despatches; the English are masters of the river and the lakes, about 40,000 men; Murray's propaganda among the Canadians and his circular against the bills of exchange; only ten thousand pounds of powder; "if I succumb it will be only in the last extremity"; with the Restigouche stores he could have secured a retreat.

reading_review.note: Read as sentences 2026-11-04 against translation_1391.md: coherent French throughout, but 94 groups lost in the binding on the versos (ff. 147v-151v): the NFA image (about 1125 px) shows only their first digit. Word count: 1,431 words, 1,303 certain, 11 probable, 97 restored, 20 unresolved: 91.8% read as sense (certain + probable), 98.6% counting the restorations. Below the 95% bar without the restorations, so read in part; a higher-resolution image (LAC deep zoom or ANOM IREL) would settle most of them.
